semantically_equivalent_models.justification: 'chatgpt-4' is semantically equivalent to 'chatbot gpt' as it represents a version of the Chatbot built on the GPT-4 architecture, which aligns with the concept of 'chatbot' utilizing GPT technology.
'chatgpt-3.5' is another variant of Chatbot utilizing the GPT-3.5 architecture. Given 'chatbot gpt', it relates directly as a chatbot utilizing the specified GPT version.
'chatgpt plus' suggests an enhanced or premium version of a Chatbot utilizing GPT technology hence it's semantically equivalent to 'chatbot gpt'.

parent_models.justification: 'GPT' is the foundational architecture for models like 'chatbot gpt', serving as a broad category under which all GPT-based chatbots would fall.

closest_parent_model.justification: 'GPT' is the most general form of the technology upon which 'chatbot gpt' is built, making it the closest and direct parental model.

child_models.justification: 'chatgpt ranker' is a derivative model which possibly applies ranking to outputs specific to a certain function of 'chatbot gpt', making it a child model.

closest_child_model.justification: Out of the child models, 'chatgpt ranker' is specifically designed around a chatbot framework, focusing on ranking capabilities which closely align with derived functionalities of 'chatbot gpt'.

sibling_models.justification: 'chatgpt-4' operates under the same parental GPT foundation and serves a similar functional role as a chatbot, hence it is a sibling.
'chatgpt-3.5' is similarly a Chatbot version beneath the same GPT architecture, placing it as a sibling.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'chatgpt-4' being the most up-to-date and advanced version aligns closely with progressive developments in 'chatbot gpt' with state-of-the-art capabilities.

unrelated_models.justification: 'gpt-j' is a specific variant of the GPT architecture that doesn't directly incorporate chatbot functionalities.
